subject: Urgent: Canary autoscaler regression impacting reserved GPU pools / customer notice
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 07:12:00 -0700
Subject: [ACTION NEEDED] Canary autoscaler regression impacting reserved GPU pools

Team — observed a canary autoscaler regression starting 07:04 PDT that prevented new canary allocations for a subset of reserved GPU pools (pools in us-west-2, M-type). Symptoms: queued allocation requests, 503s from the pool frontends, and KV cache churn. Metrics snapshot attached.

Immediate mitigations applied:
- Manual warm-up of 6 standby nodes in the affected pools (reduced queue depth).
- Fallback to pre-warmed warm nodes for customers with reserved capacity.

Root cause hypothesis: a recent autoscaler change (INF-3287) introduced a race in canary promotion under certain load patterns. Repro on staging is in progress.

Impacted customers discovered via error-rate alerts: Novastream (reserved pools), KubeSoft (minor). Novastream is the highest priority.

Next steps I recommend now:
1) Approve a temporary reservation of +8 warm nodes for Novastream in us-west-2 until we patch. (manual allocation).
2) Notify Novastream ops with short, technical notice and proposed remediation steps.
3) Schedule a rollback/patch during a mutually agreed change window.

Attachment: scaling_snapshot.png (image/png)

Marcus
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 07:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [ACTION NEEDED] Canary autoscaler regression impacting reserved GPU pools

Thanks Marcus — good triage. Ben/Monica, please see the customer-facing note below (first draft). Ben, can you send this to Novastream ops and copy me? Monica, please prepare an impact summary (token counts, minutes of degraded service) for the billing/credits ask. Karthik/Marcus — confirm you can hold the +8 warm nodes for 48 hours while engineering completes the patch.

Customer-facing draft (please edit for tone):
Subject: Immediate update: Reserved GPU pool scaling issue in us-west-2

Hi Samira / Alec,

We’re reaching out with an urgent update: this morning we observed an autoscaling regression that impacted reserved GPU pool scaling in us-west-2. Some of your workloads may have experienced brief allocation failures (manifesting as 503s) and increased queueing.

What we’ve done so far:
- Manually allocated additional warm nodes to reduce queueing and restore throughput.
- Enabled a fallback path that routes new allocations to your assured warm nodes.
- Identified the change that triggered the regression and prioritized a patch.

Planned next steps:
- We propose reserving +8 warm nodes for Novastream for 48 hours (no action required from you) while we deploy a fix and validate in staging.
- We’ll provide a written postmortem and timeline for the permanent fix within 48 hours.
- We will apply a credit for measurable impact — Monica will follow up with specifics.

We understand this is disruptive; we’ll schedule a short call to run through the timeline and answer questions.

Attachment: draft_postmortem_v0.docx

Evelyn

Hi Samira / Alec —

Quick note from Redwood: we detected an autoscaler regression impacting reserved GPU pool allocations in us-west-2 this morning. Some of your jobs may have seen transient 503s or longer queue times while we applied mitigations.

What we’ve done for Novastream right now:
- Manually added +8 warm nodes to your reserved pools (effective immediately).
- Enabled a routing fallback to those warm nodes to reduce allocation failures.
- Opened an internal ticket (INF-3287) and engineering is on it.

- We’ll hold the extra capacity for 48 hours while we verify the patch in staging.
- We’ll send a written postmortem within 48 hours and propose a credit for measurable impact.

Can we schedule a 30-minute call today at 10:30 PDT to walk through the impact and timing? If that doesn’t work, suggest an alternate time.

Hi Ben / Evelyn — thanks for the quick escalation. A few questions from our side:
1) How certain are you that the manual +8 nodes will prevent further allocation failures? We saw a spike in queueing for roughly 6 minutes before recovery.
2) What is your expected time-to-patch and rollback plan if the patch is risky?
3) We’ll need specifics for the credit calculation and a clear impact window for our finance team.

We can take a call at 10:30 PDT. Please include your engineering lead.

—Samira
Ops Lead, Novastream
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <ops@novastream.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Novastream — immediate update on reserved GPU pool scaling (us-west-2)

Samira — thank you for the quick reply and the questions; below are short answers and commitments. We’ll expand on these during the call at 10:30 PDT.

1) Confidence in the +8 warm nodes: high. The manual allocation is based on the same warm instance types already attached to your reservation; routing fallback ensures allocations target those instances first. We’ll monitor error rates for the next 48 hours and will escalate if queueing resumes.

2) Patch timeline & rollback: engineering has a staged patch that addresses the canary promotion race; estimated deploy to staging in ~6 hours, validation for ~8–12 hours, and gradual rollout to production with a canary for low-traffic customers first. If any regression is observed, we will revert the change immediately and keep the manual warm nodes in place while investigating.

3) Credit calculation: Monica will calculate a prorated credit based on minutes of degraded service and token throughput reduction across the impact window. We will share a draft credit calculation before EOD.

We’ve attached a draft postmortem for transparency; it’s a work-in-progress. Proposed change window for the patch: Wed 05/15 02:00–04:00 PDT (we can shift if that collides with your production window).

Attachment: draft_postmortem_v0.docx, buffer_capacity_proposal.pdf

Evelyn
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <ops@novastream.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 May 2028 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Novastream — credit calculation and next steps

Samira / Ben — following the impact analysis (see attached snapshot), our preliminary calculation is a prorated credit of 3.4% of May usage for the measurable degradation window (07:03–07:10 PDT on 05/14). We applied the extra +8 warm nodes immediately which mitigated further impact.

Next steps:
- We’ll finalize the postmortem and publish a public summary by EOD tomorrow.
- Patch will be deployed in the proposed window unless you request a different time.
- Confirming the 10:30 PDT call recording will include engineering (Marcus) and product (Evelyn).

Attachments: scaling_snapshot.png, draft_postmortem_v0.docx

Regards,
Monica
Customer Success, Redwood Inference
